column10: Adaptive UAV Trajectory Tracking Under Aerodynamic Disturbances Using Reinforcement Learning and Neural Model-Based Adaptation Methods
column14: This thesis presents the design, simulation training, and physical deployment of an adaptive control system for an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) capable of precise trajectory tracking under severe and time-varying aerodynamic disturbances such as wind. The control architecture combines Reinforcement Learning (RL) with an online rapid adaptation module (leveraging residual learning, meta-learning, or latent variable inference) to compensate for flight dynamics model inaccuracies and sim-to-real gaps. Following a literature review of aerial robotics adaptation techniques and sim-to-real gap mitigation, an adaptive RL policy is developed and trained in a simulation environment featuring randomized wind conditions and optional differentiable simulation. The policy performance is quantitatively evaluated and compared against standard Model Predictive Control (MPC) and baseline RL methods (such as PPO). Finally, the neural controller and reference MPC are deployed on a physical drone inside a Motion Capture (MoCap) laboratory setup to evaluate trajectory tracking errors, reaction times to artificial wind gusts, flight stability, and adaptation convergence.

column14: The goal of this thesis is to design, implement, and evaluate a hardware architecture on an SoC FPGA platform that realizes the Contrast Maximization (CMAX) algorithm for event-based cameras to estimate rotational motion parameters. To support high-definition (HD) event stream processing, the architecture incorporates external memory (DDR) management. The project begins with a literature review on rotational motion estimation, HD video pipeline architectures, and external memory controllers in reconfigurable systems, alongside a Python reference model for convergence and early-stopping analysis. A rotation model and double event-buffering mechanism are implemented and verified using a physical event camera. The target high-resolution architecture decouples event transformation from subsequent processing, employing spatial scene decomposition, dynamic task allocation across parallel processing units, and an efficient DDR controller. The complete system is deployed on an SoC FPGA and evaluated in terms of processing latency, hardware resource utilization, throughput, and motion estimation accuracy (Ground Truth error) across benchmark datasets and real-time physical tests.

Software-based modeling, quantization, and hyperparameter tuning of the SSM architecture are conducted in PyTorch. The target hardware architecture is developed in VHDL/SystemVerilog, integrating the SSM compute modules with the enhanced NAS on an FPGA. Finally, the end-to-end system is evaluated on physical hardware for classification accuracy, stability, latency, logic resource utilization, and power consumption relative to state-of-the-art baselines, concluding with a real-world application demonstration.

column10: System of underwater navigation based on sonar odometry using neural networks
column14: The subject of this thesis was to develop an odometry system for underwater vehicles, based on FLS (Forward-Looking Sonar) data and deep neural networks. As part of the research, an analysis of the physics of acoustic imaging was conducted, and a literature review in the considered field was performed. A synthetic dataset was created using the StoneFish simulation environment. Two odometry systems based on distinct approaches were developed and investigated: the adaptation of the DPVO architecture and the use of the LoFTR (Vision Transformer) model. It was observed that the DPVO architecture encounters optimization difficulties, resulting, among other factors, from the loss of information regarding the acoustic beam elevation. In contrast, the system based on the LoFTR model demonstrated high effectiveness when working with sonar data. Based on the LoFTR model, a complete odometry system was designed, utilizing image filtration, motion estimation accounting for depth changes, and trajectory stabilization using a temporal window mechanism and keyframes. In tests on simulated data, for a trajectory length of 168 m, a translation error of 1.44% and a rotation error of 0.046°/m were achieved, which translated to a final position drift of 1.76 m. At an image resolution of 776×424 pixels, the system processed data at a frequency of 2.2 Hz. The evaluation conducted on the real-world Aracati2017 dataset confirmed the algorithm's robustness to speckle noise and its ability to estimate displacement, while simultaneously highlighting challenges related to orientation estimation, as well as high sensitivity to static artifacts and the ambiguity of geometric mapping in sonar images. The proposed system surpassed the related SONIC model-based solution in displacement estimation accuracy, although it yielded weaker results in determining orientation. Following the integration of the system with reference orientation data from a magnetometer, the odometry effectiveness reached a level comparable to leading models (DISO, ISOPoT), which utilized additional velocity sensors (DVL). The thesis concludes with final remarks and an indication of potential directions for future development.

column10: Perception and control system for an autonomous vehicle model based on machine learning algorithms
column14:
This thesis presents the design and implementation of a perception and control system for an autonomous vehicle model intended for operation in laboratory conditions. The developed solution integrates a hardware platform based on a Raspberry Pi computer and an ESP8266 microcontroller with a vision system, a control module, reinforcement learning algorithms, and a web application.

The perception system uses an RGB camera and a YOLO-based object detection model. A custom dataset was prepared, image augmentation techniques were applied, and hyperparameter optimization was performed using the Optuna framework. The trained model achieved approximately 0.993 mAP50 and 0.842 mAP50:95. A Google Coral accelerator was used to improve inference performance on the target platform.

Autonomous control was developed using the Proximal Policy Optimization algorithm. The training process was carried out in a Gazebo simulation environment integrated with ROS 2. Environment randomization and sensory data disturbances were introduced during training in order to reduce the sim-to-real gap. The trained policy was subsequently verified on the physical vehicle platform.

Functional tests confirmed the correct operation of the individual modules and demonstrated that they could be integrated into a complete autonomous system. The vision subsystem showed high operational stability, while the vehicle successfully completed approximately 90% of the prepared obstacle-avoidance routes. The main limitations observed during testing were related to the physical drivetrain and the differences between the simulated and real-world platforms.

column10: State estimation of a mobile robot using event data
column14: Event cameras register local brightness changes with high temporal resolution and a wide dynamic range, making them particularly useful during rapid motion and under challenging illumination. This thesis presents a simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) system that estimates a trajectory from a stereo pair of event cameras. Events are synchronized and aggregated into exponentially decaying image representations. Points detected with GFTT (Good Features to Track) are tracked using the Lucas-Kanade method, and their depth is recovered through stereo triangulation. The resulting 3D-2D correspondences are used for PnP (Perspective-n-Point) estimation with RANSAC (Random Sample Consensus). The system uses gyroscope measurements to compensate for the smearing of structures caused by rotational motion and to determine orientation changes. To reduce drift, the pose is estimated relative to a sparse map constructed from keyframes, while place recognition enables loop closure and pose graph optimization. The system was evaluated on data from the EvSLAM and M3ED datasets, with resolutions of 640 x 480 and 1280 x 720 pixels, respectively. Across seven EvSLAM sequences, the system obtained a total ATE of 3.654 m and a total AUC of 4.996, compared with 0.817 m and 6.286 for the winning entry. For the M3ED sequences with available ground truth, the results varied depending on the sequence characteristics: the ATE values for the two evaluated sequences were 0.162 m and 25.305 m, respectively.

column10: Swarm control of unmanned aerial vehicles using reinforcement learning
column14: Drone swarms are finding an increasing number of applications, yet controlling them in environments with obstacles remains difficult, especially when decisions are made on board, based on limited information about the surroundings. This thesis extends a reinforcement learning method for swarm control that assumed exact knowledge of obstacle positions and training on a regular grid. Both simplifications were removed by replacing the idealised observation with a model of four range finders, available as a standard module for the Crazyflie platform, and by introducing diverse obstacle arrangements, including layouts resembling building interiors. Simulation studies showed that limited perception and a change in environment structure mainly reduce the safety of a controller trained under simplified conditions. The success rate alone does not fully reveal this, while suitable training conditions make the controller more robust to these changes. The controller, adapted to the capabilities of the onboard microcontroller, was then run on a real drone. After compensating for two effects not captured in simulation, it maintained a stable hover and avoided the obstacle in most flights under its control. The thesis also discusses the limitations of the adopted approach and directions for further research.

column10: Using an event camera to analyse the operation of drone propellers
column14:
This thesis concerns the use of an event camera to analyse the operation of drone propellers. The main objective was to propose, implement and evaluate an algorithm for localising rotors in an event stream and estimating their rotational speed. The work exploits the properties of event cameras, such as high temporal resolution, low latency and the ability to register local brightness changes, which make these sensors particularly suitable for analysing fast-moving objects.

As part of the work, an experimental setup was prepared using EVK1 and EVK4 HD event cameras, together with a reference measurement obtained from an optical tachometer. The developed algorithm included event filtering, localisation of regions corresponding to individual propellers, tracking of their position, event motion compensation and selection of the rotational speed that maximised an objective function based on event accumulation in a histogram. Several objective function variants were tested, together with additional extensions of the method, including centroid position correction and a simplified elliptical model intended for cases where the propeller is observed at an angle.

The experimental results showed that the EVK4 HD camera allows significantly more accurate RPM estimation than the older EVK1 model. For the EVK4 HD camera, RMAE values of approximately 0.56-1.04% were obtained, depending on the measurement height and the objective function used. The experiments also demonstrated the significant influence of lighting conditions, contrast and event polarity on propeller localisation and estimation stability. In addition, the estimated RPM signals were used to classify basic manoeuvres of a DJI Ryze Tello drone. The SVM classifier achieved an accuracy of 90.87%, although this result should be interpreted with regard to the limited amount of data and class imbalance. The conducted experiments confirm that event cameras can be an effective tool for analysing drone propeller operation, although the correctness of the method strongly depends on the quality of event data and recording conditions.

column9: Autonomiczne sterowanie rojem mikrodronów w pętli sprzężenia zwrotnego systemu MoCap
column10: Autonomous control of a micro-drone swarm within a MoCap system's feedback loop
column14:
Nano-drones (Micro Aerial Vehicles, MAVs) such as the Crazyflie are used as research platforms for autonomous flight and swarm control. Their limited payload capacity and operation in indoor environments, where GNSS is unavailable, require an external source of position information. For closed-loop control, such a system must provide a high measurement rate, sufficient accuracy, and low and predictable latency.
This thesis presents a distributed motion-capture (MoCap) system designed to provide real-time position feedback for Crazyflie nano-drones. The system uses four global-shutter cameras with infrared illumination, while each drone carries a single passive infrared-reflective marker. Image processing is performed locally on Jetson Nano units, which transmit only the coordinates of detected markers to a Jetson AGX master instead of complete images. Measurement synchronization is achieved using hardware camera triggering, frame counters, and IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol (PTP). The master reconstructs 3D positions using Linear Optimal Sine Triangulation (LOST) and filters the measurements with an Extended Kalman Filter.
The system operates at rates of up to 220 Hz and achieves sub-millimetre static positional accuracy. It was also validated in a closed-loop control experiment, where the position feedback enabled a Crazyflie to perform an autonomous reference manoeuvre. An additional experiment demonstrated simultaneous tracking of three Crazyflies. The obtained results confirm that the proposed system can provide accurate and sufficiently fast position feedback for experiments involving autonomous control of multi-drone swarms.

column9: System percepcji i sterowania samonaprowadzającego się drona
column10: Perception and control system of a self-guided drone
column14:
The importance of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) has grown significantly in recent years, driven by technological advances and the widespread use of civilian UAVs. Machine learning and developments related to deep and convolutional neural networks are highly significant for this field, as they allow for a significant expansion of the autonomy of mobile robots. The use of perception methods based on these solutions enables the analysis of a UAV’s environment and the precise navigation of such a vehicle without relying on positioning methods that require additional infrastructure.

This paper presents the implementation of a system capable of detecting a selected target, estimating the drone’s position relative to it, and planning and executing a flight path for the UAV to reach that target. An appropriate training dataset was prepared for the YOLO26n-seg model used for instance segmentation. A control script was created using Python to generate flight trajectories and control signals for the drone. To achieve this, the script also performs RGB image processing to position the drone relative to the selected target and fuses data from the camera and the onboard IMU (Inertial Measurement Unit).

The planned functionality has been achieved without the use of additional sensors, which allows the system to operate independently in conditions where it is not possible to obtain data on the UAV’s position from sources such as satellite navigation. The system’s operation was evaluated as part of a SITL (Software-in-the-Loop) simulation; however, its functionality has not been tested in a real-world environment.

column9: Dekoder sygnału dla kosmicznej komunikacji laserowej zrealizowany w układzie FPGA
column10: Signal decoder for space laser communication implemented in an FPGA system
column14: The aim of the thesis was to design, implement and verify a ground-station decoder for a satellite optical downlink in a field-programmable gate array (FPGA). The decoder was developed for the PUCHACZ student CubeSat mission of the AGH SatLab student research group. The satellite will transmit data using a pulsed 1550 nm laser with 1024-ary pulse-position modulation (PPM). The signal is received by a 0.4 m telescope with a PIN photodiode, and the stream of samples from the analog-to-digital converters is to be processed in real time by the developed decoder. The processing chain includes data acquisition from the converters over high-speed differential links with a clock-domain crossing, a correlation filter implemented without multiplications, pulse detection, slot-clock synchronization with a Doppler-shift tracking loop, 1024-PPM demodulation, a Reed-Solomon (RS) decoder over the Galois field GF(2^10) with error correction (one RS(221,205) codeword per frame) and a serial peripheral interface (SPI) output with telemetry. Every stage of the chain was verified in simulation, bit-exactly against golden models written in Python, and the complete receiver, from emulated samples to the data output, was also tested as a whole. Bitstreams covering the complete receiver were generated for the ZCU104 target platform with the Zynq UltraScale+ XCZU7EV device. The operation of the decoding chain was confirmed by measurements on the ZCU104 board, with the stimulus provided by an internal playback generator. A transmission over a real 1550 nm optical path was decoded off-line from a recorded signal waveform, using simulation. Real-time reception with the converter card remains future work.

column14: This thesis addresses the acceleration of neural networks processing irregular data, such as point clouds, on the heterogeneous AMD Versal device. The PointNetConv layer from the  ointNet family was selected and an accelerator for it was designed on the VEK280 board. The programmable logic builds edge features and performs scatter-max aggregation, while the AI Engine-ML core array executes the dense linear transformations in int16. Single-path and nine-path variants (8 and 72 cores) were implemented, and optimisations reduced their latency on the CORA citation graph (2,708 nodes, 13,264 edges) from about 18 ms to 718.66 and 389.96 𝜇s, respectively. Compared with CPU, CUDA and TensorRT implementations on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX module, the nine-path variant achieves 32.7% lower latency than the best GPU implementation, with comparable energy efficiency. The AIE kernels alone are clearly faster than the GPU, but this advantage is limited by data transfer and the programmable logic, and integrating the whole system proved to be the main challenge.

column9: System koordynacji roju dronów w środowisku zurbanizowanym z zapewnieniem ciągłości komunikacji
column10: Drone swarm coordination system in urban environment with guaranteed communication continuity
column14:
The subject of this master’s thesis focuses on the autonomous coordination of an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarm in a complex urban environment. The primary objective of the research was to develop and evaluate a system that ensures continuous communication within a multi-agent network (strictly adhering to Line-of-Sight and maximum range requirements) while simultaneously maximizing the exploration area to locate strategic targets.

This work is based on an in-depth comparative analysis of two distinct control paradigms designed for the international ICUAS UAV Competition in 2025 and 2026. The first, classical approach from 2025 was based on deterministic graph algorithms and offline trajectory planning using a simplified 2D occupancy grid. The second, innovative solution from 2026 utilized a heuristic Artificial Potential Fields (APF) method integrated with dynamic role optimization and continuous, three-dimensional Line-of-
Sight verification using k-dimensional trees and OctoMaps.

Simulation experiments conducted in ROS 2 and Gazebo environments unequivocally demonstrate the superiority of reactive methods over classical static planning. The graph-based algorithms from 2025, while guaranteeing stable connectivity, proved to be too rigid and computationally burdensome in a dynamic environment, drastically limiting the swarm’s exploration capabilities (4th place in the competition in both stages - simulation and hardware). Conversely, the implementation of heuristic methods in 2026 allowed for decentralized, instantaneous adaptation of agents to changing topological conditions and battery levels. This approach resulted in flawless mission execution, outperforming competing solutions (1st place in the competition). The obtained results confirm the thesis that in highly constrained multi-agent missions, heuristic reactive planning provides a significantly more efficient and scalable alternative to deterministic algorithms.
column15: multi-agent systems, UAV swarm, Artificial Potential Fields (APF), connectivity maintenance, heuristic algorithms, ROS 2, urban exploration

column9: Śledzenie obiektów z użyciem filtra korelacyjnego zrealizowane w układzie SoC FPGA z akceleracją w AI Engines
column10: Correlation filter-based object tracking realised on a SoC FPGA with acceleration in AI Engines processors
column14: This thesis presents the design, implementation and evaluation of an embedded visual object tracking system realised on the heterogeneous AMD Versal platform. The algorithm combines the MOSSE correlation filter with a convolutional feature representation obtained from the first layer of the ResNet-18 network, reduced to 32 channels by principal component analysis and quantized to eight bits. The processing is distributed across three types of on-chip resources: the programmable logic extracts and preprocesses the region of interest, the AI Engines vector processor array executes the convolution, the two-dimensional Fourier transforms and the spectral multiplication with accumulation across feature channels, and the application processor handles peak search in the response map, filter model update, scale estimation and orchestration. The completed system processes 38.7 frames per second at an energy cost of 12.2 mJ per frame. Evaluated on the VOT-STb2022 dataset under the multi-start protocol, it scored an accuracy of A = 0.5129, a robustness of R = 0.4279 and an expected average overlap of EAO = 0.1960. Its accuracy falls within the band of the classical correlation filters and its robustness stays below them at a fraction of the programmable-logic resources used by the closest published embedded implementation.

column10: Unmanned aerial vehicle control through EEG-based brain-computer interface
column14: The thesis presents the design of a brain–computer interface (BCI) for controlling an unmanned aerial vehicle. Brain signal acquisition was performed using an EEG amplifier and steady-state visually evoked potentials were employed as the control paradigm. The proposed BCI system enables drone control along three axes: up/down, forward/backward, and yaw rotation. A visual interface comprising six flickering stimuli with different frequencies was developed, and the optimal electrode placement was determined. Signal decoding was performed using band-pass filtering and the Sliding DFT algorithm, while classification was based on power spectrum thresholding. The accuracy, precision, and information transfer rate were evaluated and compared for systems considering one and two signal harmonics, as well as against canonical correlation analysis (CCA). The highest performance metrics were achieved for power spectrum thresholding with a single harmonic, yielding an accuracy of 79.81%, a precision of 81.81%, and an information transfer rate of 29 bits/min. Additionally, the designed system incorporates safeguards to mitigate the effects of EMG interference.

column9: Projekt i implementacja sieci typu echo state do przetwarzania szeregów czasowych
column10: Design and implementation of an echo state network for time-series processing
column14: Echo State Networks (ESNs) offer a lightweight, efficient, and scalable approach to Reservoir Computing, making them well suited for time-series processing tasks. This thesis presents the design, implementation, and evaluation of the ESN as a representative model of Reservoir Computing, with a focus on its structure, initialization methods, and quantization strategies for possible long-term time series Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) trajectory prediction. The work begins with a review of the existing literature on the ESN architecture and its fundamental components, including the description of the reservoir layer, readout mechanism and key hyperparameters. Additionally, relevant developments in the field of Reservoir Computing are considered, and the importance of long-term series prediction approach is identified. A custom ESN implementation is developed and evaluated using the most common, standard benchmark datasets, including Mackey-Glass, NARMA10 and Sunspot time-series prediction tasks. Both power-of-two quantized and non-quantized configurations are considered and their respective performance in compared. The impact of reservoir size and numerical precision on model performance is analyzed to assess the sustainability of quantized ESNs for resource-constrained applications. The network is further extended to accommodate for a more complex scenario involving long-term UAV position estimation based on sparsely placed waypoints and quantized simulation data. Evaluation of the ESN's ability to perform ling-term predictions in a real-world application is conducted. The thesis concludes with a summary of the ESN's performance across both synthetic benchmarks and application in a real-world inspired prediction task, such as UAV's path prediction, and discusses the potential of future hardware-oriented application.

column9: Adaptacja neuromorficznego akceleratora SYNtzulu do przetwarzania danych zdarzeniowych na platformie SoC FPGA dla zastosowań klasyfikacji w czasie rzeczywistym
column10: Adaptation of the neuromorphic accelerator SYNtzulu for event-based data processing on a SoC FPGA platform for real-time classification applications
column14: The growing demand for low-energy computing systems is driving the development of neuromorphic models, such as Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs), and their implementation on embedded hardware platforms, including the SYNtzulu architecture. These solutions enable low-cost and energy-efficient data processing directly near the sensors. This trend encompasses not only computational units but also modern sensing technologies, particularly event-based cameras, which, due to the independent operation of each pixel, exhibit high robustness to challenging lighting conditions. Furthermore, their sparse, asynchronous outputs, represented as sequences of events, are naturally compatible with SNN models, facilitating the creation of neuromorphic vision processing systems with very low power consumption. In the present work, a complete event-data classification system is proposed, employing spiking neural networks implemented on an SoC FPGA based on the SYNtzulu architecture. Originally, the SYNtzulu design was intended for time-series analysis, such as iECG, EEG, and sEMG signals. Here, its applicability is extended to the processing of data acquired from event-based cameras. The SNN models were trained using the SLAYER framework on the N-MNIST and CIFAR10-DVS datasets and subsequently deployed on the hardware implementation of SYNtzulu on a Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC platform available on the Kria KV260 development module. The analysis covers both the implementation of baseline fully connected networks, natively supported by SYNtzulu, as well as architectural extensions incorporating pooling layers. The proposed solution allows the processing of input images of arbitrary resolution while exploiting the sparsity of asynchronous event-based data. The configurable number of parallel neuromorphic processors enables adaptation of resource utilization and latency to application requirements. The hardware implementation consumes only approximately 10% of the available programmable logic, achieving inference times as low as 14 microseconds while maintaining classification accuracy comparable to the state-of-the-art.
column15: spiking neural networks, SNN, event-based cameras, DVS, SYNtzulu accelerator, SoC FPGA, low-power embedded systems, event-based image classification, real-time inference

column9: Szacowanie położenia i prędkości na podstawie obrazu z pojedynczej kamery zdarzeniowej przy użyciu algorytmu odometrii wizyjnej
column10: Estimating Position and Velocity from Monocular Event Cameras using Visual Odometry
column14: Event-based cameras offer high temporal resolution, low latency, and large dynamic range, making them attractive for motion estimation in robotics and autonomous navigation. This project develops, implements, and evaluates a monocular event-only visual odometry system that estimates metric 3D position and linear velocity from asynchronous event streams. Two complementary pipelines were compared: DEVO, a learning-based approach that regresses relative camera motion from spatio-temporal voxel grids using a deep neural network; and EVO, a geometric tracker-and-mapper. The evaluation pipeline includes sensor undistortion, event accumulation into temporally-binned representations, Sim(3) trajectory alignment to metric ground-truth, and velocity computation via finite differences. Experiments on publicly available event datasets use Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE) and velocity RMSE to quantify performance and investigate the impact of the event-accumulation window. Results show that DEVO consistently produces substantially lower ATE and velocity RMSE compared to EVO, which exhibits larger errors and failure on longer or more challenging sequences. A parameter study reveals a trade-off between temporal resolution and noise resilience in window sizing. The thesis concludes with a discussion of limitations and directions for future work, including deployment on hardware and inertial fusion for scale robustness.

column9: Poprawa określania pozycji pojazdów autonomicznych z użyciem odometrii wizyjnej wykorzystującej metody uczenia głębokiego
column10: Enhancing Autonomous Vehicle Pose Estimation with Deep Learning for Vision-Based Odometry
column14:
This thesis investigates the enhancement of vision-based odometry for Autonomous Surface Vehicles (ASVs) by integrating deep learning methodologies. The primary objective was to evaluate and compare the performance of a classical computer vision algorithm -- ORB (Oriented FAST and Rotated BRIEF) against a deep learning-based framework, SuperPoint, for trajectory estimation. The study utilized three distinct datasets: the standard KITTI benchmark for automotive scenarios, a synthetic maritime dataset generated via Gazebo simulation, and real-world experimental data collected by the ''Barka'' Autonomous Surface Vehicle.

The experiments consisted of a two-step comparison: first, between the baseline methods, and second, by fine-tuning the SuperPoint network on domain-specific maritime images, in order to evaluate the influence of fine-tuning the model on the pose estimation of specific datasets. Results on the KITTI benchmark showed that the deep learning approach clearly outperformed the classical one. In maritime scenes, the pretrained SuperPoint model revealed better local tracking stability compared to ORB. However, fine-tuning the model for marine environments revealed a trade-off. While the model effectively learned to filter out unstable water keypoints in favor of static shoreline features, the reduced distinctiveness of the descriptors ultimately led to higher trajectory errors than the pretrained baseline.

column9: Implementacja aplikacji end-to-end do rozpoznawania sygnału audio z wykorzystaniem neuromorficznego sensora słuchowego (NAS) i sieci GCNN na układzie FPGA
column10: Implementation of an End-to-End Application for Audio Signal Recognition Using a Neuromorphic Auditory Sensor (NAS) and GCNN Network on FPGA

The designed architecture integrates a digital model of the silicon cochlea (Neuromorphic Auditory Sensor, NAS) with a Graph Convolutional Neural Network (GCNN). The sensory component, generated using the OpenNAS tool, converts acoustic signals into an asynchronous stream of events, which is subsequently analyzed by a neural network operating on dynamic graph structures. The research process encompassed the preparation of an event-based dataset derived from the Google Speech Commands V2 corpus, model training and quantization in PyTorch, and hardware implementation on a ZCU104 SoC device using VHDL and SystemVerilog. Conducted tests confirmed the system's capability to classify voice commands in continuous mode while maintaining power consumption of 2.91 W, 10.7 μs of latency and resource utilization suitable for implementation on mid-range FPGAs. column10: Implementation of a contrast maximization algorithm on an FPGA for an event-based camera image
column14: This work presents a hardware architecture that implements the Contrast Maximization (CM) algorithm in Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) resources for event-based vision systems. CM estimates motion parameters by maximizing the contrast of an Image of Warped Events (IWE) reconstructed from asynchronous event streams. Event-based vision sensors generate sparse data with high temporal resolution and low spatial redundancy, which makes them well suited for hardware processing. The deterministic, massively parallel structure of the FPGA is leveraged to design a deeply pipelined architecture capable of high-throughput, energy-efficient processing suitable for real-time embedded applications. This work details the hardware modules responsible for event warping, contrast computation, and iterative optimization, discusses key implementation decisions, and presents the hardware-aware optimization method used in the design. Experimental results demonstrate a substantial speed and efficiency improvement over CPU- and GPU-based implementations, with motion parameter estimation executing over 200 times faster. To the best of current knowledge, this is the first hardware architecture enabling acceleration of CM algorithm computations. Its performance is evaluated in terms of processing speed, energy efficiency, and hardware resource utilization. The proposed design is validated using an event-based object tracking application. The results confirm that the architecture provides a solid foundation for real-time motion estimation in high-speed, low-power embedded systems.

column10: Utilisation of spiking neural networks with TTFS coding to event data processing
column13: 2025_Michal_Michniak_Zastosowanie impulsowych sieci neuronowych o kodowaniu TTFS do  przetwarzania danych zdarzeniowych.pdf
column14: Spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer a promising avenue for energy-efficient and biologically inspired computation, with the potential to run effectively on neuromorphic hardware. Recent advances have focused on translating conventional artificial neural networks (ANNs) into their spiking counterparts, particularly using time-to-first-spike (TTFS) coding to reduce the number of spikes and improve efficiency. However, most existing TTFS translation methods rely heavily on data-driven threshold estimation and multi-phase operations. In this work, we present a novel, fully model-driven TTFS translation approach for ReLU-PSP (Rectified Linear Postsynaptic Potential function) networks, eliminating the need for training data and employing a single, fixed activation threshold. We introduce a structural upper bound based on the ReLU1 function to control numerical stability and enable accurate inference, even with complex architectures containing residual connections. Our method is evaluated on: NCars, MNIST-DVS, CIFAR10-DVS, NCaltech101, event-based datasets, demonstrating equivalent classification accuracy to conventional ANNs.

column14: This thesis focuses on development of a quadrotor drone control algorithm using neural network. Due to better generalization capabilities and limited availability of training data, the application of PINN (Physics Informed Neural Network) was chosen. This type of model allows for effective integration of training data and physical knowledge, making it possible to achieve a good model even under conditions of limited training data availability. As part of the work, a predictive control algorithm was designed and implemented, in which the PINN model replaces the mathematical model of drone dynamics in the MPC (Model Predictive Control) algorithm. The use of this type of network aims to ensure reduced computational resource requirements and improve system adaptability to variable flight conditions. Validation of the developed approach was conducted based on checking the prediction accuracy of the network itself with known controls, simulations of the proposed MPC algorithm in given test scenarios, and finally the off-line simulation of the entire flight. Additionally, the influence of individual MPC parameters on the achieved accuracy was examined. The obtained results clearly indicate that the chosen approach can be effectively applied in practice, and that the proposed methodology allows for mitigating the disadvantages of classical approaches.

column10: An energy-efficient multitask neural network for a driver monitoring system
column13: 2025_Konrad_Pawlik_An energy-efficient multitask neural network for a driver monitoring  system.pdf
column14: Driver Monitoring Systems (DMS) are critical for modern vehicle safety, but current solutions often rely on a collection of independent algorithms to analyze a driver's state, creating an inefficient and resource-intensive pipeline. This work proposes a lightweight, multi-task learning framework that simultaneously predicts gaze direction, head pose, and facial landmarks within a single, efficient network. The framework is designed with gaze estimation as the primary objective, landmarks and head pose serving as auxiliary tasks for powerful geometric regularization. Built upon a ConvNeXt-Tiny backbone, the model achieves a state-of-the-art gaze estimation error of 4.32 degrees on the MPIIFaceGaze dataset at a low computational cost of 4.5 GFLOPs. The study has revealed that the inclusion of facial landmarks has provided a significant benefit to gaze performance, while adding head pose introduces negative transfer, degrading accuracy. The proposed framework effectively balances between high accuracy and computational efficiency, serving as a practical foundation for the development of resource-aware Driver Monitoring Systems.

column9: Detekcja obiektów z wykorzystaniem kamery zdarzeniowej oraz impulsowych sieci neuronowych
column10: Object detection using event camera and spiking neural networks
column14: Object detection is an important issue in automatic monitoring systems, robots and autonomous vehicles perception and medical diagnostics. In most current solutions, the data for detection is provided by frame-based cameras. However, they do not work correctly in environments with insufficient light levels and when recording very fast movements. In such situations, an alternative are event cameras for which the above conditions are not unfavorable.Equally important as the type of chosen sensor is how to process the data and extract the most important information from them. Nowadays, the most popular tool for this purpose are Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs). One type of ANNs are Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs). The principle of their operation is similar to the functioning of human brain neurons. Individual neurons transmit information among themselves through binary spikes. In this work, a literature review of object detection using event cameras and artificial neural network was conducted. Afterwards four variants of spiking neural networks were designed and implemented. Each of them had a different configuration of spiking layers. Models inspired by the convolutional detector YOLOv3 (You Look Only Once) were trained and validated on partial data from the Prophesee's GEN1 Automotive Detection Dataset. In addition, the impact of the chosen mathematical model of the neuron used in the network's architecture on the quality of detection was measured.The best obtained result for a fully spiking network was 0.521 mAP50 and 0.257 mAP50:5:95. Model with a spiking feature pyramid and backbone achieved 0.437 mAP50 and 0.219 mAP50:5:95, network with a partially spiking feature pyramid and backbone obtained 0.588 mAP50 and 0.298 mAP50:5:95. Lastly, model with spiking backbone achieved 0.633 mAP50 and 0.318 mAP50:5:95. In comparison, the convolutional prototype validated on the same dataset obtained 0.624 mAP50 and 0.335 mAP50:5:95 which is comparable to the spiking backbone model. In other cases, the quality of detection is slightly worse than results achieved by convolutional network, confirming a trend also noted in the literature.
column15: object detection, event camera, spiking neural network, YOLO

column9: Nawigacja modelu pojazdu autonomicznego na podstawie informacji wizyjnej
column10: Navigation of an autonomous vehicle model based on visual data
column14: Within the scope of this thesis, a selected vision-based SLAM algorithm (Simultaneous Localization and Mapping) was tested on a challenging urban environment mockup to navigate an autonomous vehicle. For the project, a mobile application was also developed, enabling control of the constructed vehicle equipped with a Jetson Xavier NX computational platform. The application provided functionalities such as activating the autonomous mode and real-time visualization of the vehicle's location on a map generated by the ORB-SLAM3 algorithm. The system was complemented by a logic module responsible for terrain exploration, maintaining the vehicle's trajectory within road lanes, and its efficient navigation using the MultitaskV3 neural network. All project objectives were achieved, and the individual system components operated correctly during testing. However, during the final comprehensive test, where the vehicle was required to autonomously navigate the entire mockup after pressing a button and subsequently travel from a selected point A to point B, certain issues arose. Due to the insufficient frame processing speed (up to 2 FPS), the vehicle occasionally collided with buildings, requiring operator intervention. Despite these limitations, both the application and the vehicle are well-prepared for further testing and improvements. A significant amount of video data was collected during the project, which can be used for further testing and system optimization.
column15: Jetson Xavier NX, ORB-SLAM3, MultitaskV3, visual navigation, SLAM, autonomous driving

column9: System równoczesnej akwizycji danych z kamery zdarzeniowej i wizyjnej
column10: A simultaneous data acquisition system from an event and video camera
column14: The presented work describes the process of creating a vision data acquisition system for automotive scenarios, consisting of a vision camera and an event camera. Firstly, a stand holding both cameras was designed, and suitable hardware was selected for algorithms implementation. Jetson Xavier AGX, powered by the vehicle's battery, was selected as a suitable platform for data processing. Software was developed to concurrently acquire data from both cameras and store them on an external memory device. Several calibration methods were tested and compared to address the issue of projecting points between corresponding images. The obtained recordings were used to assemble a dataset containing object detection coordinates for images from both cameras.The task was achieved using the YOLOv8 neural network on images from the vision camera. The coordinates of the resulting bounding boxes were transferred to the event camera images using a projection method defined in the calibration phase. This process yielded a dataset describing the location of detected objects in the images of both cameras, within time intervals determined by the moments of consecutive frame captures by the vision camera.By leveraging the timing information captured by the event camera for each recording, it became possible to associate the detection coordinates with each event registered between the consecutive frame captured by the vision camera. Thus, a dataset containing the coordinates of detected objects for each frame and registered events was obtained. This dataset can be employed for further development of detection algorithms based on event cameras.
column15: Deep Convolutional Neural Networks, Dynamic Vision Sensor, object detection, event based vision, data aquisition, event camera calibration

column9: Zastosowanie grafowych sieci neuronowych do przetwarzania danych zdarzeniowych
column10: Graph Neural Networks in event data processing
column14: Event cameras have significant potential for application in real-time object recognition and detection systems, due to their high temporal resolution, high dynamic range, and low latency. However, the unique data format recorded by these sensors poses a challenge for established vision algorithms and classical deep learning architectures designed for processing images frame-by-frame. Recent research indicates the high effectiveness of graph neural networks in processing event-based data, both in terms of prediction accuracy and computational efficiency. In this study, we investigated and compared two state-of-the-art graph convolutional network models for event-based object recognition and detection. We also proposed two custom graph neural network architectures tailored for these tasks, based on the dedicated point cloud PointNet convolution. The convolutional model, PointNet-EAGR, achieved a classification accuracy of 0.964 on the N-Cars dataset and 0.703 on the N-Caltech101 dataset, with a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.638 in the detection task on the N-Caltech101 dataset. The graph transformer model, PointNet-GPS, achieved classification accuracy of 0.977 and 0.673 on the N-Cars and N-Caltech101 datasets, respectively, and 0.637 mAP in the detection task on the N-Caltech101 dataset. Both proposed architectures exhibit significantly lower parametric complexity compared to the baseline models, while outperforming them in object detection efficiency.
column15: event cameras, graph neural networks, object classification, object detection

column9: Projekt i budowa robota na kołach szwedzkich, wykonanych w technologii druku 3D termoplastycznym poliuretanem
column10: Design and construction of a robot on omni-wheels, made using 3D printing technology with thermoplastic polyurethane
column14: This paper presents the design and construction of a mobile robot equipped with Swedish wheels made of thermoplastic polyurethane using 3D printing technology. The robot's control algorithm was implemented on the RaspberryPi ZeroW platform. An analysis of the design of the mobile platform and different types of omnidirectional wheels was carried out, considering their advantages, disadvantages and main areas of application. Available technologies and materials used during the 3D printing process were discussed. The effect of the hardness of the material in contact with the substrate, on the ability to generate friction with the substrate was examined on a prepared test bench. A comparison was also made between single and double Swedish wheels in terms of the vibrations generated during driving.

column10: An embedded perception and control system for autonomous vehicles based on convolutional segmentation and detection network
column14: The aim of the work was to design an embedded perception and control system for an autonomous vehicle based on an SoC FPGA (ang. System on Chip Field-Programmable Gate Array). The perception algorithm relied on a single, multitask, convolutional neural network for concurrent segmentation (of the road and horizontal markings) and detection (of pedestrians, traffic lights, and obstacles). Training and evaluation were performed on a custom dataset, created on a model track consistent with the one used in the FPT FPGA Design Competition, which was also built as part of this work. The robot control algorithm used the detections to stop or avoid obstacles and processed the segmentation of horizontal markings using the Hough transform to determine the speed and direction of travel. The system was implemented on the Kria KV260 platform using Vitis AI 2.5 and PYNQ 3.0. Testing was conducted on the model track with a mecanum-wheeled robotic platform. The perception system operated at a speed of 25 frames per second for images with a resolution of 512 x 320 pixels, achieving 11 frames per second along with the control algorithm.
column15: Convolutional neural networks, semantic segmentation, detection, multitask neural networks, FPGA, Zynq, System-on-Chip, System-on-Module

column9: Wydajne pamięciowo grafowe sieci konwolucyjne do klasyfikacji i wykrywania obiektów za pomocą kamer zdarzeniowych
column10: Memory-Efficient Graph Convolutional Networks for Object Classification and Detection with Event Cameras
column14: Recent advances in event camera research emphasize processing data in its original sparse form, which allows the use of its unique features such as high temporal resolution, high dynamic range, low latency, and resistance to image blur. One promising approach for analyzing event data is through graph convolutional networks (GCNs). However, current research in this domain primarily focuses on optimizing computational costs, neglecting the associated memory costs. In this paper, we consider both factors together in order to achieve satisfying results and relatively low model complexity. For this purpose, we performed a comparative analysis of different graph convolution operations, considering factors such as execution time, the number of trainable model parameters, data format requirements, and training outcomes. Our results show a 450-fold reduction in the number of parameters for the feature extraction module and a 4.5-fold reduction in the size of the data representation while maintaining a classification accuracy of 52.3%, which is 6.3% higher compared to the operation used in state-of-the-art approaches. To further evaluate performance, we implemented the object detection architecture and evaluated its performance on the N-Caltech101 dataset. The results showed an accuracy of 53.7% mAP@0.5 and reached an execution rate of 82 graphs per second.
column15: event camera, dynamic vision sensors, event data processing, graph convolutional networks

column9: Algorytmy planowania trajektorii lotu oraz sterowania dronem w znanym środowisku
column10: Drone path planning and control algorithms in a known environment
column14: The aim of this study was to review and implement selected algorithms for trajectory planning and control of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV). These were tested in an autonomous drone racing scenario. The realised approach is based on classical methods: geometric path planning and non-linear predictive control. An attempt was also made to use deep reinforcement learning for this task. Evaluation of the approaches was carried out in the PyBullet Drone simulation environment on prepared racetracks of varying complexity. The result of this work is an algorithm that sucessfuly navigate the test tracks, and an analysis of the feasibility of using reinforcement learning to realise this task.

column9: Implementacja sprzętowa obliczania map dysparycji w czasie rzeczywistym z wykorzystaniem kamer zdarzeniowych
column10: Hardware implementation of real-time disparity map calculation using event cameras
column14: In this paper, we propose a real-time FPGA implementation of the Semi-Global Matching (SGM) stereo vision algorithm based on event cameras (DVS - Dynamic Vision Sensors), which are cutting-edge sensors that only capture brightness changes that take place in the scene being viewed. As a result, they have low latency and perform efficiently in a variety of illumination situations. Due to the different data format in the described system, the generation of event frames onto which incoming events within a specified time interval are projected is used. The implementation on Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) devices allows for the development of numerous vision systems that work in real-time and have minimal power requirements. To reduce latency of generated disparity maps, modified SGM implementation is used to process pixels in the 4ppc format, which provides results comparable to the original design.
column15: SGM, DVS, event camera, FPGA, real-time processing, stereo vision

column9: Detekcja i rozpoznawanie sygnalizacji świetlnej na podstawie danych wizyjnych i zdarzeniowych
column10: Traffic light detection and recognition using video and event data
column14: In this work the possibility of using event cameras in the traffic light detection and classification system was considered. For this purpose, three algorithms were developed, which were based on the YOLOv7 network. First of them is based on visual information from Huawei P20 Pro. The next one uses data from the event camera Samsung DVS Gen3, and the last one operates on both of these sources simultaneously. Solutions were compared with each other to determine their speed and accuracy. The F1-score measure of the algorithms on the test sets was 98.6%, 93.6% and 98.8%, respectively. Based on obtained results, it can be concluded that use of an event camera is possible, but does not bring significant benefits.

column10: A low-latency test platform using signal processing acceleration in an FPGA
column14: Test platforms, used for real-time hardware-in-the-loop simulations, reduce the cost and time to market. This thesis describes the implementation of selected signal processing algorithms in the VHDL hardware description language and running them on an FPGA device. The system used a NI 7857R PCI Express card, which was equipped with an FPGA from Xilinx's Kintex-7 family. The module calculated scalar values for each input signal, such as minimum, maximum, arithmetic mean, root mean square, and the number of samples per signal period. The prepared solution will be part of a modular test platform for the verification of additional flight control systems. The verification carried out confirmed the implementation of the assumed functionality.

column9: Nawigacja dronem na podstawie informacji wizyjnej w środowisku pozbawionym sygnału GPS
column10: Vision-based drone navigation in GPS-denied environments
column14: Reinforcement learning has an increasingly important role in robot control and simulation plays a key role in this process. In the field of drones, a large number of scientific papers have also been published on this topic.The subject of this thesis is the preparation of two different autonomous drone control systems based on an algorithm in the field of reinforcement learning. The first one was prepared for the Dodge Drone Challenge, which involved flying a distance of 60 m ahead, while avoiding obstacles in the form of floating balls. The second system was designed to autonomously fly forward and avoid the trees encountered in a forest. This was done basing only on the readings from a rotating LiDAR sensor.The thesis presents the preparation of environments in three different simulators: Gazebo, Flightmare and a custom one. The last two were used to train Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) agents responsible for calculating the value of control signals. Gazebo was used to test the drone control scripts, which were based on the Robot Operating System. The work also describes the architecture of the prepared solutions, encountered problems, and the implemented software, which was written in Python and C++.The second system was first tested in the Gazebo simulator, and then it was put into operation in reality. The drone successfully flew through both virtual and real forests.

column10: Traffic sign classification with event-based data and Spiking Convolutional Neural Networks
column14: The study investigated the issue of using neuromorphic computing, specifically convolutional spiking neural networks (CSNN) to perform traffic sign classification (TSR) using event-based data from an event camera.The architecture of the CSNN network was based on the Lenet model. A collection of event camera recordings "Prophesee 1 Megapixel Automotive Detection Dataset was used for the learning process. Implementation and simulation studies were carried out using the Lava environment. Despite performing a variety of experiments, it was not possible to obtain a working classifier using this approach.

column10: Object classification using deep and quantum neural networks
column14: Quantum neural networks are an emerging technology that can be used in many applications, including computer vision. This thesis presents a classification system for handwritten digits and road signs implemented using a hybrid quantum-classical neural network based on a convolutional network architecture. Experiments indicate that currently these networks do not outperform classical deep convolutional neural networks, but especially for the German Traffic Sign Recognition Benchmark dataset, they provide an accuracy of about 90% and are definitely a promising solution for advanced machine vision.

column9: Sterowanie pojazdem autonomicznym z wykorzystaniem informacji wizyjnej i detekcyjno-segmentacyjnej konwolucyjnej sieci neuronowej
column10: Autonomous vehicle control using visual information and a detection-segmentation convolutional neural network
column14: This work presents an autonomous vehicle control system, where the perception subsystem was based on a detection-segmentation convolutional neural network. An NVIDIA Jetson Nano eGPU with a camera was used as the computing platform. The information about the road area, lane line area and object presence (such as another vehicle) was acquired by using the YOLOP architecture. This information was used to implement driving within a chosen lane, obstacle avoidance and following of a preceding vehicle (platooning). The created system performed properly on test images and sequences, as well as during autonomous driving around the used track. It worked with the speed of 3.7 frames per second.

column9: Sterowanie autonomicznym dronem wyścigowym na podstawie informacji wizyjnej
column10: Autonomous drone racing control based on visual information
column14: The project designed and tested various methods for controlling an autonomous racing drone. These included both typical solutions based on PD controllers, as well as methods using reinforcement learning. In addition, algorithms for locating the drone in space and a system for determining its dynamic state in real time based on its model were also presented. These solutions were implemented to allow the multi-rotor to fly autonomously through a series of gates that determine the route to be taken. They were similar to those used in autonomous drone racing. The operation of the entire system is as follows: At first, based on information from the camera, the multicopter locates the gates and determines its position relative to it. Then the data on its position and orientation go to the algorithm, which, based on the drone's model, determines its current dynamic state. The information about it then goes to the control algorithms, the output from which is sent to the flight controller in the multicopter. The created system was installed on a drone built specifically for this project. It has a carbon fiber frame, an Nvidia Jetson Nano on-board computer with a connected camera, on which the algorithms described earlier were run, as well as a flight controller controlling the motors and a differential GPS module. Tests of the system's performance for different configurations (using different control solutions) were carried out to check the quality of the given solutions' performance and compare them.
column15: Autonomous drone, reinforcement learning, dynamic state determination, dynamic system control, Nvidia Jetson Nano, vision system, Python programming language

column9: Szybkie zliczanie elementów z wykorzystaniem kamery zdarzeniowej.
column10: High-speed item counting using an event camera
column14: In this thesis a high-speed object counting stand was designed and built to simulate the conditions that can occur in the industry. It consists of two key parts, a chute that allows one to regulate the number of falling objects by controlling a motor that generates vibrations, and a vision system used to count falling objects. The Prophesee's event camera, the Metavision EVK 1 HD, is used. The stand is equipped with a software-implemented PID controller, which allows to maintain the set flow or, for example, to portion products. The regulator sets the PWM filling control of the motor, taking as feedback the number of counted objects. In the final part of the project, a series of experiments were carried out to evaluate the quality of the system and the correctness of the solution.

column9: ATLAS Local Trigger Interface - rozwój implementacji sprzętowej, weryfikacja oraz testy
column10: ATLAS Local Trigger Interface - firmware development, verification and testing
column14: ATLAS is the largest particle detector ever constructed at the European Organization for Nuclear Research CERN. The detector gathers 60 million megabytes of data per second. To reduce this enormous flow of data, a complex Timing and Data Acquisition (TDAQ) system was developed. The subject of this thesis is the ATLAS Local Trigger Interface module. The ALTI is a part of the ATLAS Level-1 Trigger system. It is a newly developed module which replaces the four previously used TTC interface modules, also called the TTC "Legacy'' system (LTP, TTCvi, TTCex, LTPI), for the incoming Run 3 period. The thesis presents the ALTI module's final firmware and its place in the Timing Trigger and Control (TTC) distribution system. This work focused on the ALTI firmware development and its functionalities verification. The project’s goal to deploy a firmware version that covers all TTC Legacy system functions was achieved. The firmware development process was based on the VHDL language and Vivado 2020.2 environment. The implemented functionalities were thoroughly tested with behavioral simulations as well as hardware tests. To achieve that, the Mentor ModelSim simulation testbench and Python-based hardware testing environment were developed and improved. The ALTI firmware was also compared with the Legacy system in terms of the Level-1 Trigger Accept (L1A) latency. The new module was processing triggers 7.12 ns faster than the old interface system.
column15: FPGA, ATLAS, TDAQ system, ALTI, TTC System

column9: Symulacja “hardware-in-the-loop” na potrzeby weryfikacji aplikacji przeznaczonych dla bezzałogowych statków powietrznych
column10: Hardware-in-the-loop simulation for unmanned aerial vehicles applications verification
column14: In this work, a „hardware-in-the-loop” simulator for the verification of vision algorithms dedicated for unmanned aerial vehicles was proposed and designed. The possibility of testing solutions running on embedded computing platforms in a virtual environment leads to a significant acceleration of the prototyping of such systems. It also allows to exclude in the initial phases of testing problems associated with the transition from the stage of the software model to hardware implementation. In this work, a review of the literature treating about similar simulation solutions has been carried out. A number of issues about the construction of aerial vehicles and their control were also developed. In the next part, two versions of the simulator based on the Matlab/Simulink environment were prepared - one of them using Unreal Engine and the other one based on Three.js - JavaScript library. The implementations were tested based on „human-in-the-loop” model and on algorithms: landing on a~platform and flying through a~series of gates. The conducted tests, although limited in scope, allowed to draw a conclusion on the usability of the prepared simulators in the process of development and verification of embedded vision systems.
column15: 3D visualization, algorithms verification, embedded vision system, simulator, hardware-in-the-loop simulation

column9: Detekcja obiektów z wykorzystaniem kamery zdarzeniowej
column10: Object detection using an event camera
column14: In this work, selected algorithms for pedestrian and vehicle detection by event camera were implemented and tested. These techniques included the use of popular 2D representations of event data, such as event frame, or time surface. Furthermore, an approach using grayscale image reconstruction from the event stream was also presented.In the first stage, the appropriate form of the event packet is prepared, then the proper detection is performed by using a deep convolutional detector known as YOLOv5, which is one of the state-of-the-art solutions in the field of object detection. The evaluations were carried out on a dataset consisting of selected sequences from Gen1 Automotive Detection Dataset, DDD17, DDD20 datasets and event simulation of several dozen BDD100K videos.The final part of the work is dedicated to optimize the inference speed by creating more compact versions of the trained neural networks. Some well-known methods such as knowledge distillation and neural network pruning have been used. However, the evaluation results indicate a decrease in detection quality that is significantly greater than that of the analogous procedure for data from traditional frame-based cameras. The best-performing algorithm is characterized by an accuracy, expressed as AP, of about 0.48. This is not surprising, since the nature of event sensors makes object detection clearly more difficult. This is especially true for the smallest objects when the amount of information is very limited due to the sparse representation of event data.
column15: Deep Convolutional Neural Networks, object detection, event-based vision

column9: Automatyczna rejestracja przebiegu gry w brydża sportowego
column10: Automatic registration of a duplicate bridge game
column14: In this work, the implementation of an application for automatic registration of a duplicate bridge game is presented. It is based on a vision system that processes images recorded by a system of two cameras directed at the table where the game takes place.The first stage of the task is the detection of elements used during play - cards and bidding calls. For this purpose, two YOLOv4 deep convolutional neural networks were used. During the training process, which was carried out using an automatically generated dataset, we obtained a detector characterised by more than 99.9% accuracy on the test set. The second part of the system is responsible for analysing the obtained information and, based on the rules of the game, reconstructing its course.The prepared application has been tested on video collected during bridge competitions and is characterised by its high accuracy. Minor modifications and hardware acceleration could make it possible to use the system for preparing live broadcasts of bridge competitions.
column15: Deep Convolutional Neural Networks, vision system, object detection, duplicate bridge

column9: Detekcja obiektów z wykorzystaniem głębokich sieci neuronowych zrealizowana na wbudowanej platformie obliczeniowej
column10: Object detection using deep neural networks implemented on an embedded computing platform
column14: This work presents the full process of designing hardware implementation of a detecton system based on deep neural networks for the 2021 DAC SDC competition. The aim was to design a solution with high accuracy, high throughput and low energy consumption. The requirements and assumptions of the competition and the target platform - "Avnet Ultra96 V2" were initially discussed, as well as the available classic solutions and solutions based on neural networks, especially energy-saving solutions, were reviewed. Next, the process of designing the network architecture is presented, along with training and quantization, and the implementation of a hardware accelerator as well as attempts to optimize energy consumption are described. The obtained result was the detection accuracy of 0.7015, measured with the IoU coefficient, with a throughput of 72.7 fps and energy consumption of 2739 J for 52500 images.
column15: Deep Convolutional Neural Networks, vision system, object detection, Quantized Neural Networks, hardware accelerator

column9: Rekonstrukcja informacji 3D przy użyciu kamery zdarzeniowej
column10: 3D reconstruction with an event camera
column14: In this work, the implementation of 3D reconstruction system with the usage of data provided by event cameras is presented. This type of sensors register events for each pixel independently and asynchronously, however only the change in the intensity of the incident light is detected. This results in high temporal resolution, low latency, and low energy consumption. At the same time, due to the atypical data format, it is impossible to use ''classic'' methods of image processing and analysis. In this study, four methods of 3D reconstruction (two classical and two based on neural networks) were implemented and evaluated. Various representations of event data were also used -- event frames, reconstructed frames, and voxel grids. Algorithms were evaluated on a publicly available data set and the obtained results were compared with methods presented by research teams that participated in the CVPR 2021 competition. In terms of the most important metric MAE (Mean Absolute Error), the obtained results turned out to be several times worse, but a slight improvement was observed for the 1PE (1 Pixel Error) metric. By using classical algorithms, the obtained results turned out to be better than with usage of neural networks. The fastest method`s processing time for pair of frames was 1.88 seconds.
column15: 3D reconstruction, vision system, stereovision, event camera

column10: Locating and counting objects using data fusion from unmanned aerial vehicle sensors
column14: This study developed and implemented an object (apples) localization system utilizing data fusion from sensors installed on an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). The system relies on advanced object detection and tracking methods, including YOLO, SORT, Deep-SORT algorithms, and single-object tracking (SOT) and multi-object tracking (MOT) techniques, ensuring high precision and performance.The proposed solution integrates data from a GPS RTK localization system and utilizes a drone platform equipped with an Nvidia Jetson computing unit, enabling real-time program execution. The system was implemented within the Robot Operating System (ROS) environment using Python and C++ programming languages.Additionally, the study presents the process of adapting the drone platform to the task requirements, detailing hardware specifications, module communication schemes, and the configuration of the Pixhawk The Cube Orange flight controller. Tests and performance analysis evaluated the effectiveness of the applied approaches, including Tracker OpenCV, Tracker MOT, and Tracker SOT with GPS localization. A comparison was also made between the performance of two YOLO versions: v8 and v11.
column15: unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), drone, object detection, YOLO, SORT, Multi-Object Tracking, Single-Object Tracking, DeepSORT, GPS RTK, Nvidia Jetson Xavier NX, ROS, depth camera Realsense D435i

column9: System percepcji i sterowania drona transportowego
column10: Perception and control system for a transport drone
column14: In recent years, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) have become an inherent part of modern technology. They have found application in various fields, such as transportation or photography. They are also widely used in the military industry, where they have to tackle moving in space with disrupted satellite positioning signals. This thesis presents the design and implementation of a perception and control system for a transport drone, which tackles GNSS-denied environments. The topic was inspired by one of the Droniada 2024 competitions. The main objective was to design a UAV that moved in the environment composed of ten square platforms. Basic perception sensors of drones, such as the IMU, magnetometer and pressure sensor, were extended by an RGB camera. Its image was processed by vision algorithms. Their purpose was to extract data necessary for positioning based on detected objects from the competition map. The implemented software was tested in the Gazebo simulator in accordance with the Software-In-The-Loop techology, on a specially preperad test scenario. Designed perception module evaluation stated high effectiveness. Furthermore, the entire system was assessed based on the competition task, where the criteria were as follows: number of correctly transported balls and the delivery time. Achieved sufficient results, which proved designed drone systems accuracy.
column15: unmanned aerial vehicle, perception systems, control systems, GNSS-denied environment, vision systems, map positioning, SITL, ROS, PX4

column9: Detekcja przeszkód z wykorzystaniem kamery zdarzeniowej
column10: Obstacle detection with an event camera
column14: In this work an object detection system - obstacles for a mobile robot (drone) using an event camera (DVS - Dynamic Vision Sensor) was created. This sensor was applied to ensure correct operation under different lighting conditions. Ways of solving the issue in other designs available in the literature were analysed and a custom detection algorithm was created. A SiL (Software in the Loop) simulation was prepared to test the algorithm in daylight and night conditions in variety of scenes with obstacles. A drone equipped with a simulated event camera was deployed in the scene of testing environment. Tests of the obstacle detection system were carried out using the SiL method and available datasets with DVS data. Their results were presented and discussed.
column15: DVS, event camera, obstacle detection, object detection, drone, simulation, Software in the Loop, Gazebo

column9: Integracja wbudowanej platformy obliczeniowej z kontrolerem lotu bezzałogowego statku powietrznego
column10: Integration of an embedded computing platform with the flight controller of the unmanned aerial vehicle
column14: In recent years, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV) have become widely used in an ever-increasing range of applications. It can be largely attributed to the developments made in the field of machine learning, especially deep and convolutional neural networks. This fact allowed their use for the purpose of autonomous operation of mobile units such as the UAV. By integrating this functionality with the manual control system it is possible to transfer the control over the UAV to the onboard processing unit for the purpose of precise navigation and the continuation of its mission in the event of a disruption or a complete loss of radio connection between the UAV, and its operator. This work presents the implementation of a system containing both hardware and software elements allowing for the integration of the Jetson Nano embedded computing platform with a UAV for the purpose of autonomous object detection and tracking while preserving the manual control functionality. A dedicated switching circuit was developed, allowing the user to pick one of two control signal sources, as well as a Python script for carrying out object detection and control tasks. YOLOv7-tiny was utilized as the object detector and the detection results together with PID controllers were used for correcting the position of the UAV. The described functionality was implemented to only use the data acquired from the onboard camera in order to render the system's performance independent of potentially unavailable or incorrect data in difficult conditions (such as GPS or barometer readings). Despite this, the developed system carries out the intended task with satisfactory accuracy.
column15: convolutional neural network, perception, embedded AI, eGPU, UAV

column10: Object tracking utilizing fusion of vision and thermal imaging implemented in an SoC FPGA using the Vitis AI tool
column14: This thesis presents a vision system combining images from a visual and a thermal camera. The calibration process of the two cameras is carried out using the OpenCV library. The system, implemented in Python, performs object detection using the YOLOv3 detector and tracks the objects with the SORT algorithm. The YOLO convolutional neural network model was trained and evaluated on the PST900 image dataset. The Vitis AI 2.0 tool was utilized to implement the detector on the SoC FPGA platform. The vision system was tested on an eGPU (Nvidia Jetson Xavier NX) and SoC FPGA (Xilinx Kria KV260). The computation time and detection quality were tested. On the SoC FPGA system, a significant reduction in computation time was observed, but with a decrease in quality.
