column9: Naprowadzanie autonomicznego, bezzałogowego statku powietrznego na cel
column10: Guiding an autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle towards a target
column14: This bachelor thesis focuses on the design, implementation, and evaluation of an algorithm for guiding an autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle towards a ground target using visual information. The developed algorithm combines MOSSE and DSST correlation filters with features extracted from a convolutional neural network, ensuring high tracking accuracy and robustness in varying environmental conditions.The algorithm was tested in the Gazebo simulation environment, enriched with obstacles and dynamic elements to replicate real-world scenarios. The test results confirmed the effectiveness of the solution both in simple and complex environments.The work provides a foundation for further research, including the implementation of the algorithm on SoC FPGA, and is applicable to military operations, rescue missions, and environmental monitoring. The developed solution demonstrates potential for tasks requiring autonomous tracking and guidance in real-time operations.
column15: unmanned aerial vehicle, UAV, drone, autonomus guidance, tracking algorithm, visual object tracking, machine vision, correlation filter, convolutional neural network

column9: Ewaluacja impulsowych sieci neuronowych z wykorzystaniem narzędzia Neurobench
column10: Evaluation of spiking neural networks using the Neurobench tool
column14: The aim of the project was to compare effects of the change in spiking neural networks training algorithm from standard error backpropagation algorithm, to EXODUS - error backpropagation through time algorithm. The assessment has been undertaken, to check if extending the training domain to include time domain, would result in improved mAP metric value of spiking nets. Within project we modified already available implementation of spiking neural networks trained to perform object detection tasks, changing LIF neurons from spikingjelly framework to LIF neurons from sinabs-exodus framework. Neurobench framework has been utilized within evaluation process. Training resulted in significant improvement in terms of net performance, proving higher efficiency of the training with EXODUS. Obtained results were compares with state-of-the-art models.

column9: Wykorzystanie konwolucyjnych grafowych sieci neuronowych w metodach SLAM
column10: The use of convolutional graph neural networks in SLAM methods
column14: In a simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) system, a reliable visual odometry module is an essential component, as it is necessary for accurately perceiving the environment. In this thesis, we explore the potential of graph convolutional neural networks to enrich SLAM methods. We analyze a spectrum of deep learning approaches, from networks employing pretrained convolutional models to those with customized convolutional layers working on raw image data. Although the results of these investigations are unsatisfactory, resulting in less than optimal performance, they offer invaluable insight into the complex interplay between neural network design and visual navigation tasks. Additionally, the integration of the well-known SuperGlue network is addressed, illustrating its potential to improve the accuracy of odometry. This research emphasizes the significance of integrating advanced neural network architectures to strengthen SLAM systems, which may pave the way for future breakthroughs in the field.
column15: Visual Odometry, Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM), Convolutional Graph Neural Networks, Trajectory Estimation, Deep Learning in Robotics, Feature Extraction, Perception, Pose Estimation

column9: Badanie możliwości zastosowania otwartoźródłowych soft rdzeni RISC-V w systemach kosmicznych o znaczeniu krytycznym
column10: Feasibility Study of Open-Source RISC-V Soft Cores for Mission-Critical Space Systems Applications
column14: With the growing privatization of the space industry, access to space has become more democratic. Avionics, including onboard computers, have become a significant part of the overall cost of satellite missions due to the decreasing cost of launching satellites into orbit. The aim of this study was to investigate the potential use of consumer-grade Field Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGA) as an alternative to expensive, specialized microcontrollers. As part of the study, a RISC-V architecture-based onboard computer processor for a nanosatellite was implemented inside an FPGA. Current consumption measurements were taken, and the resistance to errors induced by ionizing radiation was evaluated. The research findings indicate that the system in geostationary orbit radiation conditions would experience an average of 0.68 errors per year. The study identified the potential use of consumer-grade FPGA systems and RISC-V architecture as a promising alternative for the nanosatellite onboard computer, which requires further research.
column15: FPGA, RISC-V, space technology, artificial satellites

column9: Realizacja trajektorii lotu drona z wykorzystaniem algorytmów MPC
column10: Realisation of drone trajectories using the MPC algorithm
column14: In this study, an analysis of Model Predictive Control (MPC) algorithms was conducted for the task of trajectory realization by unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The implementation included three versions of the MPC controller: nonlinear, based on successive linearization, and using the quasi-linear parameter varying (qLPV) model. Each of these algorithms was evaluated in the PyBullet Drone simulation environment on prepared test trajectories. The conducted research included assessment of trajectory tracking accuracy, analysis of computational complexity, and testing for disturbance robustness. The obtained results confirmed the functionality of each of the three controller versions, and the conclusions made it possible to a more comprehensive understand of their features and potential application areas.

column10: Drone formation flight control algorithms
column14: Swarms and drone formations are increasingly finding various applications in many areas of life. Significant advancements in autonomy in robotics and rapid progress in the field of control algorithms have opened the doors to the development of controllers for systems with multiple agents, capable of satisfying diverse needs, including obstacle avoidance. In this paper, selected solutions for controlling drone formations are presented. These solutions, proven successful in real-condition tests, involve the implementation of a drone speed controller and ultimately a formation controller using swarm algorithm. These algorithms draw inspiration from the principles of potential fields and inherit concepts from Reynolds' work. Proposed solution was evaluated, successfully conducting a photorealistic simulation of the flight of six drones through two different tracks with obstacles. The work highlights the strengths and weaknesses of the chosen drone formation flight control algorithm and indicates possible future directions for its development.

column9: Wykorzystanie wizyjnego sprzężenia zwrotnego w algorytmie lądowania drona
column10: The use of visual feedback in a drone landing algorithm
column14: This work proposed a system designed for automatic landing on a detected platform. The PX4 flight control software was utilised with the iris model of an unmanned aerial vehicle and Software in The Loop (SITL) simulation framework. The system was developed using ROS (Robot Operating System) and the MAVROS library, which facilitated communication between the system and the drone. Initially, the landing algorithm relied on a PID controller with altitude-dependent parameters. The application, in this form, functioned correctly for all prepared test scenarios. Subsequently, an attempt was made to integrate a Discrete Kalman Filter (DKF) into the system, which did not result in success.

column9: Akceleracja algorytmu detekcji odpadów przy pomocy karty Xilinx Alveo U50
column10: Acceleration of garbage detection algorithm with Xilinx Alveo U50 card
column14: This engineering diploma thesis presents the acceleration process of deep neural network algorithms using the Xilinx Alveo U50 card.The first part discusses theoretical issues related to convolutional neural networks, quantization and acceleration of AI models on different hardware architectures. This was followed by a process of configuring the card and preparing the Vitis AI environment, including the installation of the necessary software. The process of running models started by focusing on the problem of object classification. The accuracy and data processing throughput of the simple MNIST classifier and the ResNet-50 model were investigated.The resulting frame rate was 23,000 and 577 FPS (frames per second), respectively. In the following part, the problem of object detection was considered. The YOLO architecture (\textit{You Only Look Once}) was mainly used here. Several research threads were raised. It was confirmed that used dataset does not affect the speed of the model. Then, three successive versions of YOLO (v2, v3 and v4) were put together to compare their performance. For the test cases considered, the results with the highest confidence factor were returned by the latest, fourth version. However, data were processed fastest by the oldest version. In addition, the throughput of the selected YOLOv4 model was compared for CPU, GPU and Alveo U50 architectures. The FPGA card achieved twice as many frames per second as the better of the two GPUs used. The entire implementation path was presented, from training the model, quantization, compilation and running it on a accelerator. The detection results obtained were at 97\% mAP, while the throughput was identical to other YOLOv4 models.The conclusion presents the findings of the research, describes the encountered problems and presents further opportunities to develop the work.
column15: CNN, AI, FPGA, Vitis AI, hardware acceleration, object detection

column9: Detekcja pieszych z wykorzystaniem kamer zdarzeniowych
column10: Pedestrian detection using event cameras
column14: Pedestrian detection is an important issue in advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), autonomous vehicles and advanced automated video surveillance systems (AVSS). Traditional frame cameras are used in such solutions, but they do not work properly for insufficiently lit environments, large brightness range on the scene and the occurrence of very fast movements. Event cameras can also be used to implement such systems. Due to their characteristics (low latency and high dynamic range) event-based sensors can detect people quickly and under adverse lighting conditions. In this work two network architectures were analyzed and implemented: Event-based Asynchronous Sparse Convolutional Network and the YOLOv7 detector. Both models were trained and tested on sequences from the 1 Megapixel Event Camera dataset.The results obtained from the Event-based Asynchronous Sparse Convolutional Network, despite the change of various model parameters and techniques for slicing the input image into smaller fragments, were unsatisfactory. The best result obtained during testing was 0.033 in the AP metric (Average Precision). Another approach based on the YOLOv7 detector and a two-dimensional representation of events in the form of SAE (\textit{Surface of Active Events}) was also proposed. A significantly better performance of 0.9476 AP was obtained for this model. The implemented detector works correctly for single objects, but due to YOLO limitations, some pedestrians occurring in larger groups remain undetected.
column15: object detection, event-based camera, YOLO, asynchronous neural networks, sparse convolutional neural network

column10: Object tracking using classical methods and deep neural networks
column14: This thesis is devoted to the issue of classical object tracking methods. As part of the undertaken activities, a comprehensive description of popular "classic" object tracking methods was prepared, such as KLT, MeanShift, CamShift, particle filter and correlation filter. They were implemented in Python and compared with methods using Siamese neural networks and tracking by detection. The algorithms were evaluated on sequences downloaded from the VOT challenge database using the methodology of this competition. The obtained results allowed the observation of differences in the effectiveness of individual methods and their characteristics. The summary indicates further directions of development.

column9: Dron rozpoznający osoby na podstawie obrazu twarzy
column10: A drone that recognizes people from facial images
column14: The aim of the thesis was to develop a system using a DJI Tello EDU drone to autonomously track and follow an identified person, while enabling gender and age classification. The design involved the drone moving freely in open space, without colliding with obstacles. The aim was to make a precise manoeuvre to approach a spotted person, make a photograph and then return safely to the starting point. After the flight, the age and gender of the person in the photo were classified. Due to the technical limitations encountered, it was not possible to realise the free movement of the drone, however, the other aspects were successfully implemented.

column10: Static obstacle avoidance for a drone using an event camera
column14: The aim of the thesis was to develop an event camera based control system for a flying drone controller. The drone should be able to safely traverse a course comprised of static obstacles while avoiding them and maintaining a safe distance from each of them. It was assumed that drone is flying on arbitrarily chosen, fixed altitude and is unable to fly over the detected obstacles. Proposed solution was tested with a computer simulation in MATLAB Simulink. The utilised event stream was extracted from a regular video file using a dedicated, machine learning based, simulation software.

column9: Autonomiczny dron śledzący pojazdy w środowisku miejskim
column10: Vehicle tracking in an urban environment using an autonomous drone
column14: Nowadays unmanned aerial vehicles, also known as drones, are very popular. Both within the scientific community and the commercial sector, research on flying vehicles is constantly being conducted due to their high potential for development of various applications, i.e. infrastructure inspection or geodetic data collection. For this reason, many different competitions are held, creating the right conditions for modeling and testing new solutions, and thus stimulating teams from around the world to work on the subject. In this paper, an example of a simple solution was presented, which is an introduction to the first part of the UAV Chase Challenge Competition. The project includes a software model designed in the ROS operating environment. As part of its implementation, the control module of the four rotors and the flight stabilization was made, as well as an application containing a simple vision track for detection and tracking the designated target. To visualize the environment and measure the distance, a depth camera with a resolution of 1280 x 960 and a frame rate of 30 Hz was used, placed on the front of the drone, facing forward. The model has been simulated and tested in the Gazebo 11 environment, on the Linux Ubuntu 20.04 operating system.

column9: Monitorowanie zmęczenia kierowcy z wykorzystaniem kamery zdarzeniowej
column10: Driver fatigue analysis using an event camera
column14: Event cameras (DVS) are modern vision sensors that use in their genesis knowledge of engineering and biology. Their construction was inspired by structure of the human eye, the information is send in the form of pulses - events. Distinguishing features for DVS are: high dynamic range, wide temporal resolution, low power consumption and independent work of pixels. Due to above, it is possible to use event cameras in adverse lighting conditions, for instance in observation of the vehicle driver. State of fatigue is hard to be classified or defined, however it has significant impact on our abilities, by reducing perception or reflex. Information about level of fatigue can be accesed by analysis of length and freequency of blinking, dynamics of head motions or occurrence of yawning. The greatest challange of this paper was implementation of monitoring and level of fatigue analysing application. During program operation, temporal characteristics are examined (with a help of previously prepared ideal models of blinking, mouth opening and closing), also algorithm inspired by Gaussian Blob Tracking was used to track driver's face. At the end, it is made a decision about driver's fatigue level and his driving ability. Important feature of presented application is low memory usage, fluctuating between 20 and 50 [MB], depending on accuracy of prepared patterns. That score is very satisfactory, especially compared to~competetive solution as neural networks. The final stage was to measure system effectiveness. Testing recordings was prepared from a diversed group of people. During tests, one averaged model was used for blinks and second one for yawns. Specialization of program by its adaptation to individual people was not utilized. Quantity of detected blinks oscillated at around 73%, yawning, on the other hand was correctly recognized in 67% cases. Relatively low efficiency of presented algorithm stems from the nature of event cameras, and the fact, that these modern sensors are not well known yet. Moreover, limited ability to acquire resources from vast group of people of different races, genders and age resulted in imperfection of prepared models.
column15: event cameras, vehicle driver monitoring, fatigue analysis, events temporal characteristics, face tracking

column9: Wykrywanie, rozpoznawanie i śledzenie obiektów na boisku piłkarskim z wykorzystaniem systemu wizyjnego
column10: Object detection, recognition and tracking on a football pitch using a vision system
column14: This paper presents a vision system responsible for object detection, recognition and tracking on a football pitch. To develop such a system, video sequences from static cameras were used. To detect person-like objects, a background subtraction algorithm, morphological operations, and contour analysis were applied. To classify them into groups (two different teams and referees) and to detect the ball, convolutional neural networks were used. The tracking problem was divided into two separate problems: single-object and multi-object tracking. They were solved using the mean-shift algorithm and Kalman filter accordingly. A 75% detection and 99,5% classification accuracy were achieved on the test set.
column15: football video analysis, object detection, object classification, object tracking

column9: Wbudowany system do segmentacji i detekcji obiektów zrealizowany na platformie Zynq SoC
column10: Embedded system for object segmentation and detection implemented on the Zynq SoC platform
column14: The aim of the work was to design an embedded system for simultaneous segmentation (drivable area and lane line) and object detection (pedestrians, traffic lights, obstacles). The algorithm was implemented with the help of a single, one-stage convolutional neural network, based on U-Net. Model training and evaluation was done using the Barkley Deep Drive 100K dataset. The trained model was then compiled to run on the Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC chip with the help of the Vitis AI development stack, and run on the Kria KV260 System-on-Module development board. The resulting application enabled simultaneous detection and segmentation at speeds of approximately 11 frames per second. In addition, system operation was analyzed on a miniature road prepared as part of the work, in accordance with the requirements of the FPT FPGA Design Competition.
column15: convolutional neural networks, semantic segmentation, detection, FPGA, Zynq, System-on-Chip, System-on-Module

column10: Time optimization of a racing drone flight over a closed track using reinforcement learning.
column14: The work presents an usage of reinforcement learning in order to design an autonomous control system for an unmanned aerial vehicle. The intended target is to achieve a decision-providing model of drone control with the use of physic simulation. This result is accomplished by obtaining total flight time reduction techniques. The system's task is to take advantage of available information provided by distance and inertial sensors. Choice of appropriate flying maneuvers is supposed to enable maintaining high average velocity and avoiding collisions with walls. The conducted experiments which involved the Soft Actor-Critic algorithm did not provide satisfactory results. The partial success is limited to the temporal capability of achieving in-air stabilization.
column15: reinforcement learning, Soft Actor-Critic, autonomous steering, drone racing, trajectory planning, physics simulation

column9: Klasyfikacja obrazów z wykorzystaniem grafowych sieci neuronowych
column10: Image classification with graph neural networks
column14: Recent works indicate a wide field of applications for Graph Neural Networks (GNN) in many deep learning tasks. Image classification models based on Graph Convolutional Networks (GCN) appear particularly promising. This work describes Graph Neural Networks, as well as other types of neural networks in general. It also presents some of GNN vision applications and proposes an image classification model based on image segmentation and GCN architecture, which achieves 95.01%, 63.34% and 74.29% accuracy on MNIST, CIFAR10 and GTSRB datasets respectively. It finally explains how Graph Neural Networks can be applied in the zero-shot classification problem in which sets of training and test classes are disjoint. To meet this condition, two architectures were proposed, both using word vectors embeddings to catch semantic relations between classes and represent them in knowledge graph. These models achieve 45.10% and 13.19% accuracy on the AwA2 (animals with Attributes 2) and CUB (Caltech–UCSD Birds 200) datasets.
column15: Graph Neural Networks, Graph Convolutional Networks, image classification, zero-shot classification

column9: Detekcja i rozpoznawanie znaków drogowych z wykorzystaniem kamery zdarzeniowej
column10: Traffic signs detection and recognition using an event camera
column14: The purpose of the presented work was to develop a road sign detector that uses data from an event camera. The final model was based on the deep convolutional network YOLOv4, well known for its good accuracy-to-speed trade-off. To deliver the data to the detector in the form of two-dimensional images, three 2D representations of the data from the event cameras were used -- event frame, event frequency, and exponentially decaying time surface. The road sign representations and labels were obtained from the events shared by the company Prophesee, in the 1Megapixel dataset. The best results were achieved by the model using the third of introduced 2D representations as input. The highest value of the average precision (mAP) metric in this case was 0.58. Due to the asynchronous nature of the problem, highly dependent on the time context, it was decided to propose additional model evaluation metrics, taking into account the detection of unique objects over the entire test recording, instead of the prediction evaluation for each frame. The work includes the implementation of a road sign classifier that distinguishes different types as well. Due to the lack of training data, the Video to Event model was used to generate a simulation of event frames based on camera recordings from the CURE-TSD set. To generate labels for video frames, the YOLOv4 model was trained for detecting road signs in colour (RGB) images. Its final recall on the test dataset was 0.94. Data acquired via the described process was used to train the final model, that was supposed to detect and classify road signs using event data. The best network model with the YOLOv4 architecture reached average precision (mAP) value of 0.69

column9: Segmentacja jezdni i detekcja wybranych znaków poziomych przy użyciu czujnika wizyjnego oraz platformy eGPU NVIDIA Jetson
column10: Road segmentation and detection of selected horizontal signs using a vision sensor and the NVIDIA Jetson eGPU platform
column14: The project presents the implementation of an algorithm for autonomous driving of robot on Mecanum wheels. Methods of road segmentation and detection of road markings were used, in particular those that use deep neural networks. Additionally, edge detection algorithms (Canny's algorithm) and straight lines (Hough transform) were used. The developed algorithm was implemented on the NVIDIA Jetson computing platform. The vehicle was controlled using visual feedback. The result was the autonomous driving of the robot around the city model. The vehicle detected upcoming curves and pedestrian crossings. On this basis, the car made both turns and stopped in front of the transverse line preceding the pedestrian crossing. The operation of the algorithm was verified in tests - both in the photos of the city model and during test drives. Additionally, the influence of image distortions on the segmentation performance was analyzed.

column9: Detekcja i rozpoznawanie znaków drogowych z wykorzystaniem rekonstrukcji obrazów z kamery zdarzeniowej
column10: Traffic sign detection and recognition using event camera image reconstruction
column14: Event cameras are a new type of sensor based on the action of the human eye. They are characterized by a high dynamic range, high time resolution and low power consumption. Compared to traditional vision cameras, they work better in unfavorable lighting conditions, enable the registration of fast movement and low latency. The information returned by the camera, called events, forms into an asynchronous stream, which makes it impossible to use existing algorithms for sign detection. The solution to this problem turned out to be the methods allowing to reconstruct images in shades of gray from the event camera.This work presents the implementation of a system which enables the detection and recognition of road signs based on reconstructed images from an event camera. In order to perform the reconstruction, the FireNet convolutional neural network was used, which is one of the newest solutions enabling image reconstruction. On the other hand, the YOLOv4 network was used as a road sign detector, which is characterized by high accuracy and relatively low computational complexity. Two separate models were trained, respectively, for colour and grayscale images from the GTSDB (German Traffic Sign Detection Benchmark) dataset. As the base for the recordings from the event camera, the DSEC (Stereo Event Camera Dataset) collection and the Driving Event Camera Dataset were used. Time and quality tests of both algorithms were carried out using the NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2060 computing platform. The time needed to perform the reconstruction from the collected events in 1 ms and 10 ms was 19.15 ms and 52.25 ms, respectively. The proposed solution cannot be used in real time while implemented on a GeForce RTX 2060 graphic card. One solution to this problem would be to reduce the amount of information used for image reconstruction, which would reduce its precision. Qualitative detection tests were carried out using the mAP@0.5IoU and mAP@0.75IoU metrics based on an own test set consisting of 20 reconstructed frames. Better results were achieved by the model trained on gray images. For the mAP@0.5IoU metric, a high mAP value of 87.03% was obtained, while for mAP@0.75IoU it was 64.17%. The average detection time per frame was 30.86 ms, regardless whether the model was trained in colour or grayscale images.
column15: traffic signs, event camera, reconstruction, detection

column9: Implementacja sprzętowa rektyfikacji i obliczania map dysparycji metodą SGM dla strumienia wizyjnego o rozdzielczości 4K
column10: Hardware implementation of rectification and disparity map computation with the SGM method for a 4K video stream
column14: The paper describes the architecture and implementation of a stereo vision system for a 4K resolution video stream. The solution includes image acquisition, rectification and estimation of the depth map (disparity). The semi-global matching (SGM) algorithm was used to determine the disparity map, which is considered to be one of the best methods for solutions that require real-time processing. Due to the large data stream related to 4K resolution, the 4ppc (4 pixels per clock) vector format was used. The system implementation and the necessary modifications of the algorithm for processing in the 4ppc format to meet the timing constraints were described. The system was implemented and verified on the VC707 board card with the Xilinx Virtex-7 FPGA chip. It allows the generation of disparity maps from HDMI 4K (3840×2160 pixels) @ 30Hz video stream with 64 disparity levels.
column15: SGM, FPGA, 4K, Ultra HD, real-time processing, stereo vision

column9: Detekcja obiektów z wykorzystaniem czujników wizyjnych i głębi oraz platformy eGPU NVIDIA Jetson
column10: Object detection using vision and depth sensors and the NVIDIA Jetson eGPU platform
column14: The goal of the work was to design and implement an algorithm to detect road obstacles, pedestrians and traffic lights with the use of vision and depth sensors. It allowed the control of a vehicle equipped with Mecanum wheels and the NVIDIA Jetson eGPU computing platform.The use of the Mask R-CNN network allowed to obtain an algorithm with a very high efficiency, which was confirmed by tests on many camera shots on a city model and on images with added interference. The refresh rate of the program, equal to about 1.5 FPS (frames per second) turned out to be problematic, because the system's response time would be longer than that of a human. However, the value was still sufficient for the purposes of the project.The result of the work was a robot driving on a miniature model of the city, recognizing pedestrians, obstacles and traffic lights in three colors. The vehicle, when approaching the detected objects, reacted to them by performing appropriate maneuvers.
